subject: SilverLine private cluster ops sync: landing & IO governance
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: SilverLine Labs <infra@silverline.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: SilverLine private cluster ops sync: landing & IO governance

Alex / SilverLine ops team —

Thanks for confirming the pilot next month. Attached is the preflight worksheet we use to capture site inventory and IO constraints (silverline_preflight_template.xlsx). For the kickoff I want to make sure we capture three things up-front so the on-prem rollout doesn't get stuck mid-sprint:

1) Node footprint: expected worker count, GPU types, and whether NVMe is local or shared (we've seen performance regressions when caching sits on slower blockstores).
2) Network topology & egress: will the cluster have an outbound NAT via a single egress appliance, or per-rack egress? Any private peering (MPLS/VPN) expectations?
3) Retention & backups: retention windows for model artifacts and object-store snapshots + s3-compatible endpoint locality.

Can you fill sections A–C in the attached and return by EOD Friday? Grace will take the lead on IO sizing, and Karthik will scope node classes and storage classes based on your answers. We'll use this note as the checklist during the site visit.

Proposed next step: 30-min technical sync Wed 9/22 at 10am PT to review the completed sheet and confirm on-site checklist. If that works I’ll send a calendar invite.

Thanks —
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Field Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachment: silverline_preflight_template.xlsx
From: Alex Romero <alex.romero@silverline.io>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2027 18:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SilverLine private cluster ops sync: landing & IO governance

Hi Stephanie —

Thanks, received. I'm attaching a quick site inventory export (site_inventory_sample.csv) to seed your template — it's from our inventory DB, not final but should help. Quick clarifications from our side:

- NVMe is local on the GPU nodes (2 x 3.2TB NVMe per host). We also have a small iSCSI block pool for long-term artifacts.
- Egress: currently a single egress appliance per colo room; we'll need to discuss per-rack NAT if Redwood recommends it for cross-tenant routing.
- Retention: object snapshots retained 90 days; model artifacts kept 180 days.

We can do Wed 9/22 10am PT — works for me. Also, are there standard power / PDU requirements you want us to include? Our facilities team needs exact power draw estimates before the site visit.

Regards,
Alex Romero
Senior Infrastructure Engineer
SilverLine Labs

Attachment: site_inventory_sample.csv
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2027 07:14:00 -07:00
Subject: FW: SilverLine private cluster ops sync: landing & IO governance

Pinned notes before the call (internal):

- NVMe: local NVMe on GPU hosts is great — we should size KV cache to use one of the NVMe devices and preserve the other for local scratch. Ask if NVMe is mirrored or single-disk.
- iSCSI pool: confirm IOPS and latency SLA; plan to avoid using it for KV cache or hot model artifacts.
- Egress: single egress appliance per room means we'll likely recommend an extra NAT instance per rack for isolation if they plan multiple tenants later (mention cost tradeoffs).
- Power: request per-rack PDU max draw and whether breakers are shared across racks. If they can provide nominal W/host we can compute thermal & power headroom in our BOM.

Action items for Wed sync:
1) Stephanie: confirm meeting invite and ask Alex to bring the facilities contact or share PDU spec sheet before the call.
2) Grace: prepare two IO sizing scenarios (conservative / aggressive) with expected token throughput and cache hit % assumptions.
3) Monica: draft an initial storage-class mapping for NVMe vs blockstore and an eviction policy suggestion for KV cache.

Karthik
Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: SilverLine private cluster ops sync: landing & IO governance

Alex — thanks for the quick return and the inventory extract, that helps a lot. I've created a short agenda for Wed's 30-min sync and attached the Redwood networking checklist PDF (redwood_onprem-networking-checklist.pdf) for your facilities team to review ahead of time.

Agenda (30m)
- 0–5m: Introductions and scope (Stephanie)
- 5–12m: Inventory review & NVMe details (Alex)
- 12–20m: IO sizing scenarios (Grace)
- 20–26m: Power & egress / NAT options (Monica + Karthik)
- 26–30m: Next steps, on-site dates, and preflight deliverables

Two asks before the call:
1) Can you share per-host nominal power draw (Watt) and PDU model?
2) Please confirm whether NVMe is configured with RAID/metadata mirror or presented as single devices to the OS.

I sent a calendar invite for Wed 9/22 10:00am PT (please accept). If facilities can't join live, please send PDU spec sheet into the Drive link above.

Speak soon —
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Field Solutions
Redwood Inference
